word: Well, as Apple grew, we hired someone—who I thought was very talented—to run the company with me.
meaning: 隨著蘋果的成長，我們聘請了一個——我認為非常有才能的——人來和我一起經營公司。
example: As the company expanded, he brought in someone he believed was highly talented to help manage it.
hint:
中文解釋：埋下悲劇伏筆——引進的人才，後來成為導致他離開的關鍵人物。
1) hired (v.): 聘用；syn: brought in; ant: fired
2) talented (adj.): 有才能的；syn: skilled; ant: incompetent
pronunciation: Measured: as AP-ple GREW | we HIRED some-ONE | who I THOUGHT was ver-y TAL-en-ted | to RUN the COM-pa-ny.

word: And for the first year or so, things went well.
meaning: 起初大約一年的時間，一切都很順利。
example: In the beginning, the partnership worked smoothly for about a year.
hint:
中文解釋：短暫的平靜期——為後面的分裂做對比。
1) first year (n.): 第一年；syn: initial period; ant: later years
2) went well (phr.): 進行順利；syn: worked out; ant: fell apart
pronunciation: Calm: And for the FIRST YEAR or SO | things WENT WELL.

word: But then our visions of the future began to diverge.
meaning: 但後來，我們對未來的願景開始出現分歧。
example: Over time, they started to disagree about the direction the company should take.
hint:
中文解釋：核心矛盾點——願景分歧是很多合夥人關係破裂的根本原因。
1) visions (n.): 願景、對未來的想像；syn: goals; ant: agreement
2) diverge (v.): 分歧、走向不同方向；syn: split apart; ant: converge
pronunciation: Turning point: But THEN | our VI-sions of the FU-ture | be-GAN to di-VERGE.

word: And eventually we had a falling out.
example: In the end, their relationship broke down completely.
hint:
中文解釋：直接點明關係破裂的結果，語氣簡潔有力。
1) eventually (adv.): 最終；syn: in the end; ant: immediately
2) falling out (n.): 鬧翻、關係破裂；syn: dispute; ant: reconciliation
pronunciation: Short + final: And e-VENT-ual-ly | we had a FALL-ing OUT.

word: When we did, our board of directors sided with him.
meaning: 當這件事發生時，董事會站在了他那邊。
example: When the conflict came to a head, the board of directors supported the other person.
hint:
中文解釋：關鍵的權力轉移——董事會的選擇決定了 Jobs 的命運。
1) board of directors (n.): 董事會；syn: executive board; ant: (n/a)
2) sided with (phr.): 站在…那邊、支持；syn: supported; ant: sided against
pronunciation: Decisive: When we DID | our BOARD of di-REC-tors | SIDED with HIM.

word: And so at 30 I was out, and very publicly out.
meaning: 於是，在我三十歲時，我被趕了出去——而且是非常公開地被趕出去。
example: At thirty years old, he was removed from the company in a very visible and public way.
hint:
中文解釋：「publicly out」強調這不只是內部事件，而是在全世界面前發生的羞辱。
1) at 30 (phr.): 在三十歲時；syn: at age thirty; ant: at a young age
2) publicly (adv.): 公開地；syn: openly; ant: privately
pronunciation: Blunt: at THIR-ty | I was OUT | and VER-y PUB-lic-ly OUT.

word: What had been the focus of my entire adult life was gone, and it was devastating.
meaning: 我整個成年生命的重心就這樣消失了，那是毀滅性的打擊。
example: The thing he had devoted his whole adult life to was suddenly taken away, and it was crushing.
hint:
中文解釋：情感最重的一句——不只是失去工作，而是失去了人生的全部意義與重心。
1) focus (n.): 重心、焦點；syn: center; ant: distraction
2) devastating (adj.): 毀滅性的；syn: crushing; ant: minor
pronunciation: Heavy: the FO-cus of my EN-tire a-DULT life | was GONE | and it was DEV-as-tat-ing.

word: I really didn't know what to do for a few months.
meaning: 有好幾個月的時間，我真的不知道該怎麼辦。
example: For months after, he had no idea how to move forward.
hint:
中文解釋：坦誠的低潮描述——失去方向的迷茫，讓聽眾感同身受。
1) didn't know (phr.): 不知道；syn: had no idea; ant: knew exactly
2) a few months (n.): 幾個月；syn: several months; ant: a few days
pronunciation: Lost: I REAL-ly did-n't KNOW | what to DO | for a FEW MONTHS.
